## `ComposableTuringIDModels.jl`

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
- The proof of concept, a library of parts over `Turing.jl`
- Three kinds of part. An infection model, an observation model, and
  prior models nested in the slots of both
- Parts carry their own priors
- A model definition does not know about the data. One definition
  simulates and fits

::: {.attribution}
Registered in General at v0.1.1 ·
[github.com/EpiAware/ComposableTuringIDModels.jl][ctim] ·
Abbott et al., *Composable probabilistic models can lower barriers to
rigorous infectious disease modelling*, in CDC clearance
:::
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](../figures/composable-structure.png){height="700px"
fig-align="center"
fig-alt="Four applications drawn as graphs over a band of shared parts"}

::: {.attribution}
Four illustrative applications, not implementations. The incubation
period model appears in all four and the latent infection model in
three
:::
:::
::::

## `as_turing_model`

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
```julia
@model function as_turing_model(model::IDModel, y_t, n)
    infections ~ as_turing_submodel(model.infection_model, n)
    I_t = infections.I_t
    Z_t = infections.Z_t
    obs ~ as_turing_submodel(model.observation_model, y_t, I_t)
    generated_y_t = obs.y_t
    expected_y_t = obs.expected
    return (; generated_y_t, expected_y_t, I_t, Z_t)
end
```

::: {.attribution}
`src/compose.jl:53-62`, `main` at `011169f`, one comment line removed ·
61 `as_turing_model` definitions across 45 files in `src/`, counted
2026-08-12
:::
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
- `IDModel` holds two parts, an infection model and an observation
  model
- Every part is a plain struct with one method of `as_turing_model`
- A part that holds another part draws it as a submodel
- A part is identified by the method it implements, not by its place in
  a type tree

::: {.attribution}
Last line is `docs/src/design.md:18-20`
:::
:::

## ARIMA(2,1,1)

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```julia
ar2 = AR(;
  damp = [truncated(Normal(0.2, 0.2), 0, 1),
          truncated(Normal(0.1, 0.05), 0, 1)],
  ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(std = HalfNormal(0.1)))

ma1 = MA(;
  θ = [truncated(Normal(0.0, 0.2), -1, 1)],
  ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(std = HalfNormal(0.1)))

# the AR's innovation slot now holds the MA process
arma21 = @set ar2.ϵ_t = ma1
arima211 = DiffLatentModel(arma21, Normal(0, 0.2); d = 1)
```

::: {.attribution}
Run against `main` at `011169f` for this talk · `@set` is
`Accessors.jl`, not ours · Keywords track `main`. The paper's artefact
pins an earlier release, where these were `damp_priors`, `θ_priors` and
`std_prior`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
![](../figures/composable-arima.png){height="500px" fig-align="center"
fig-alt="MA(1) inside AR(2) inside ARMA inside ARIMA, then Poisson"}

::: {.callout-note}
`AR` was never told that `MA` exists.
:::

## `as_turing_submodel`

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
```julia
# a component writes its parameter slot once
damp ~ as_turing_submodel(model.damp, p; prefix = true)

# what is in the slot picks the method
as_turing_submodel(m, args...; prefix = false) =
    to_submodel(as_turing_model(m, args...), prefix)

as_turing_submodel(d::Distribution, ::ModelShape;
    prefix = false) = d
```

::: {.attribution}
Two of the three `as_turing_submodel` methods,
`src/base/priors.jl:65-82`, reformatted to fit and with the `::Bool`
annotations dropped. The third takes a vector of priors · The slot line
is `src/base/priors.jl:25` · The `AR` example is
`src/latent_models/models/AR.jl:40-43`
:::
:::
::: {.column width="44%"}
- A slot takes a fixed prior or a whole process
- A `Distribution` draws one scalar. A process draws a path of length
  `n`
- `AR(damp = Normal(...))` is a constant coefficient,
  `AR(damp = RandomWalk())` a time-varying one
- The component that owns the slot is not changed either way
:::
::::
